headline: South Korea has cleared 20 walking humanoid robots to work alongside people in four industries, in a pilot exempt from safety rules written for fixed industrial robots.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a government allows humanoids to share factory floors with workers, but it is a limited pilot of 20 robots.
importance_line: Workers in semiconductor, car and shipbuilding plants will share floor space with walking robots, and the pilot is meant to show how reliable humanoids are in real work, but it is a limited trial of 20 robots with safety conditions, not a general approval.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports that South Korea's trade and industry ministry, through its regulatory sandbox committee on 13 Oct 2026, granted robot maker Robros a demonstration exemption to place 20 AI-powered bipedal humanoids in shared work areas at Nepes (semiconductor parts), Sungwoo Hitech (auto body parts), HD Hyundai Samho (shipbuilding) and Delivery Lab (refrigerated logistics), where existing rules required safety fences and barriers around industrial robots. The exemption is conditional on risk assessments and safety measures, and the data collected will be used to write future safety standards for humanoids.
